leading_positions.synthesis: Four of eight members prefer a two-name Katori and Ye prize for the optical lattice clock. They share the view that the magic-wavelength invention is specific and original, that Katori's concept and Ye's record-accuracy programme give a clean two-person attribution, and that the result is reproduced across laboratories and species with consequences for the redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of constants. They also share the same main reservation, overlap with the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize, and the open question of whether to wait for the SI redefinition. They differ in how they got here: Olsson moved from B042 and the chair from B021 (IceCube) after reading the other ballots, while Kroll and Lindroth held B014 first. Kroll raises a possible recusal or disclosure question over his time in Hall's laboratory, and Olsson raises a possible institutional link through Japanese exchanges that she says she must check.

Three members prefer a Kane, Mele and Molenkamp prize for the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators. They share the argument that this is a closed prediction-and-observation chain (Z2 invariant, then helical edge transport in HgTe wells in 2007), reproduced for nearly two decades, and that it is conceptually broad and mature. They also share the same reservations: the HgTe proposal by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang is not credited, the three-dimensional topological insulator work lies outside the candidate, and the 2016 prize may be read as covering neighbouring ground. They differ on emphasis only: Mehlig explicitly notes that Zhang is deceased and that HgTe edge quantization is imperfect, Johansson stresses imperfect quantization in longer channels, and Danielsson leaves open that the 2016 overlap could move him to B014. Mehlig moved here from a close second after reading the ballots. All three list B014 as an alternative.

One member prefers a Georges, Kotliar and Vollhardt prize for dynamical mean-field theory, as a non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons with three decades of testing against data and wide use through DFT+DMFT. This is a single-member position. Its distinctive difficulties are that it honours a method rather than a discrete discovery, that Metzner's infinite-dimension work is omitted by the three-name ceiling, and that quantitative predictivity depends on double-counting and interaction parameters. Eriksson himself acknowledges that B016 and B014 are more decisively theory-meets-experiment and lists both as alternatives, and discloses field proximity.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members name one of only three ballots as their preferred configuration (B014, B016 or B018), each as a single-part prize, and B014 and B016 appear as alternatives in most files, so the live choice appears to be between a metrology invention and a topological-matter prediction with experimental confirmation.
B014 is an explicit alternative for the three B016 supporters, and B016 is an explicit alternative for Kroll, Lindroth and the chair (B014 supporters) and for Eriksson.
Members across the B014 and B016 positions agree that both are mature, independently reproduced results, and that neither is premature.

Every member who discusses B014 names the same reservation, overlap with the 2005 Hall and Haensch prize and the 2012 Wineland prize, and every member who discusses B016 names the same reservation, the uncredited Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang HgTe proposal and the 2016 topological-phases prize.
Several members state that they have not verified priority and chronology details against the nomination files, so those details should be treated as recollection rather than established facts.
scientific_disputes: Whether the optical lattice clock (magic-wavelength trapping and many-atom interrogation) is a new principle and discovery, as B014 supporters hold, or an extraordinary refinement of the frequency-comb and ion-control programme already recognised in 2005 and 2012, as Danielsson and several reservations in the B014 files put it.

Whether a new classification of electronic phases by topology (B016) carries greater conceptual reach than a precision-measurement invention (B014), as Danielsson, Johansson and Mehlig argue, or whether the metrology achievement is the more concrete and consequential one, as Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and the chair argue.

Whether the 2016 prize for topological phase transitions and Haldane-type Chern insulators leaves room for Z2 time-reversal-invariant insulators. Mehlig and Danielsson regard them as distinct and complementary, while Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson and Mehlig all record the overlap as a risk.
How seriously to weigh imperfect HgTe edge-channel quantization, raised by Johansson and Mehlig, against the reproduction of the quantum spin Hall effect in other materials.

Whether a method such as dynamical mean-field theory (B018) can be treated as a discrete discovery for the purposes of the prize, as Eriksson argues, or whether the committee should prefer a discrete theory-meets-experiment result.
attribution_disputes: B014: the split between Katori's concept and first realization and Ye's record-accuracy and many-body clock work, and whether Lemonde, Ludlow, Takamoto, Lemke, the ion-clock groups and PTB, Paris and NIST teams have claims outside the two credited names. Kroll and Lindroth see the credit as clean, while Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and the chair all flag these possible additional claims.

B016: the HgTe route was proposed by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, who are not credited, and Zhang is deceased. The three-dimensional topological insulator work (Fu, Kane and Mele; Moore and Balents; Hasan) is outside the candidate. Danielsson, Johansson and Mehlig differ in how far this makes the three-name prize incomplete or unfair, and Johansson says B014 would be the cleaner two-person allocation if the HgTe attribution cannot be defended.
B018: Metzner's infinite-dimension limit versus the Georges and Kotliar impurity mapping, with the three-person ceiling forcing the omission of one name.
B021: the allocation among Halzen, Karle, Spiering and the wider IceCube collaboration remains unsettled in the chair's own account.
B042 (Olsson's opening first choice, now an alternative): the credited names omit the scanning-transmission corrector work of Krivanek and collaborators.
maturity_disputes: B014: whether to wait for the formal redefinition of the SI second before awarding, raised as an open point by Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and the chair, versus the view that the demonstrated 10^-18 performance and reproduction already suffice.

B016: no member argues it is premature, since it has been stable for almost two decades, but Danielsson, Johansson and Mehlig note that some would read it as redundant after 2016 and as incomplete without the 3D topological insulator work.
B018: Eriksson notes that no one has argued that DMFT is immature, and its three decades of testing are not contested in the other files.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Kroll (B014): documented doctoral time in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, in the same research environment as Jun Ye's group, with no recorded collaboration with Katori or Ye. He asks the chair to decide whether this requires recusal or disclosure only.
Olsson (B014): a University of Tokyo fellowship and long-running exchanges with Japanese universities, flagged as a possible institutional connection to Katori that she has not yet checked.

Olsson (B042): works in electron microscopy, serves as president of the International Federation of Societies for Microscopy, and says she should be recused from advocating or voting on B042, her opening first choice.

Johansson (B009): works in superconducting circuits and waveguide QED at Chalmers, directs WACQT and has documented ties to Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson, so would recuse or decline to advocate on B009. She also notes the proximity of the 2025 laureates' visit to Chalmers for any superconducting-circuit candidate.
Eriksson (B018): discloses that DMFT and DFT+DMFT are close to his own research, with no documented tie to Georges, Kotliar or Vollhardt.
Pearce, chair (B021): IceCube is in the chair's own field of astroparticle physics, with no recorded tie to its credited names. No conflict is recorded for B014.
Danielsson and Lindroth flag only field proximity (B001 and the atomic-physics candidates B014, B022, B008, B005 respectively) and not a recusal issue. Mehlig reports no conflict.
questions_for_round2: Kroll's Boulder connection to Hall's laboratory: does it call for recusal from B014 or disclosure only, and should the same question be answered for Olsson's possible Japanese institutional link before any B014 vote is counted?

If B014 and B016 are the two principal candidates, which criterion should decide between them: breadth of conceptual reach, clarity of attribution, or breadth of support across all eight members, and can members who support one say what would move them to the other?

For B014: can the citation be worded so that the lattice clock is clearly distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and does the committee wait for the redefinition of the SI second or treat the demonstrated 10^-18 performance as sufficient?

For B014: how should the credit be weighed between Katori's magic-wavelength concept and Ye's accuracy programme, and are the claims of Lemonde, Ludlow, Takamoto, Lemke or the ion-clock groups strong enough to threaten a two-name prize?

For B016: can a three-name credit without Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang be defended, given that Zhang is deceased and that the HgTe proposal preceded the observation, and does the 3D topological insulator work have to be part of the story?

For B016: does the 2016 prize for topological phases and Haldane-type Chern insulators leave Z2 insulators and helical edge states as a distinct subject, and how much weight should imperfect HgTe edge quantization carry?

For B018: can the three-person ceiling be reconciled with Metzner's foundational contribution, and does a method qualify as a discovery or invention in the sense required, as Eriksson argues, or is the discrete-discovery standard the committee prefers?
Are there members who would favour a different configuration (for example a two-part prize combining distinct achievements), given that B014 already uses two of the three available names?
summary.chair_observation: The eight round-1 files record four explicit supporters for B014, three for B016 and one for B018, each as a single-part prize, with B014 and B016 recurring as alternatives. The disagreement is about what kind of achievement the Prize should reward and how much weight clean attribution and prior recognition (2005, 2012, 2016) should carry, not about the maturity or reproducibility of either leading candidate. The disclosed items on Kroll and Olsson need to be settled before any later count, and nothing here is a ruling or an inference about votes beyond what the eight files state.
